subject: commit message wording and issue linking
body:
Verified by reading 25 consecutive master commits (2026-08-22 .. 2026-08-11).

WORDING: jsoup's maintainer writes bug fixes DECLARATIVELY, describing the new correct behaviour rather than announcing a fix. Only 2 of 25 subjects contained "Fix" ("Fix XML doctype system ID quote serialization", "Fix foreign content breakout parsing"). Other clearly bug-shaped commits read: "Make hostless HTTP(S) URLs fail resolution and cleaning", "Escape supplementary characters for non-UTF charsets", "Align text-state tokenization with the HTML spec", "Preserve XML nodes in W3CDom conversion", "Apply the default 512 max stack depth to the XML parser". A keyword net keyed on fix/bug/resolve WILL miss most of them. Do not read absence of fix keywords as absence of bug fixes.

ISSUE LINKING: PR number is appended in parentheses at end of subject, e.g. "(#2580)". A referenced upstream ISSUE may also appear inline before it, e.g. "Add Elements.before(Node) and after/prepend/append(Node) #953 (#2567)" — there the fix is PR #2567 for issue #953. Both are plain #nnnn GitHub refs.

HISTORY SHAPE: linear. All 25 commits observed had isMerge=false, so PRs are squash-merged to master. One commit == one landed change, which is good for mining: no need to unpack merge commits.

NOISE: dependabot[bot] authored 5 of the 25 commits observed ("Bump X from A to B (#nnnn)"). These carry many issueRefs (harvested from the dependency's own changelog, sometimes 40+) and touch neither source nor tests. They inflate any net that keys on issue references and should be filtered by author==dependabot[bot] before adjudication.

subject: history tool windowing behaviour
body:
Two behaviours of the history_* tools that cost calls to rediscover. Both observed this run; re-verify before relying on them, they may be build-specific.

1. history_list_commits IGNORES 'since'. since=2026-08-19 and since=2025-08-22 returned byte-identical commit lists, both reaching back to 2026-08-11 with scanned=25/truncated=true. Date-bounded windows are NOT expressible. Use maxCount only, and derive the date span by reading authorDate off the returned commits.

2. history_candidates' maxCount is SCAN DEPTH (commits examined), not a cap on candidates returned. Verified: maxCount=20 -> scanned=20 with 8 STRUCTURAL candidates; maxCount=60 -> scanned=60 with 56 candidates. There is no candidate-side cap parameter. Consequence: to respect a candidate cap of N you must choose scan depth such that (match rate * depth) ~= N, and on jsoup the LEXICAL match rate is ~70% of ALL commits, so depth 60 already yields 56 candidates. Budget accordingly.

3. history_list_commits with maxCount>=400 overflows the tool-result size limit (113,001 chars) and is written to a file the agent may have no shell to read. Keep maxCount <= ~25 per call if you need to actually read subjects; ~180-280 chars per commit entry.

subject: maven build image and phases
body:
Verified working at HEAD (46b620860af930eedc193a705eaf7cea5aec89a6): baseImage maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-17 (plain eclipse-temurin:17-jdk has no mvn binary -> MISSING_TOOLCHAIN, exitCode 127). buildTool maven, no mvnw. Compile-only gate: `mvn -B -q compile`. Test+coverage (pom has no jacoco plugin configured, invoke goals from CLI): `mvn -B -q org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin:0.8.13:prepare-agent test org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin:0.8.13:report`. Both verified to succeed via jvm_build_probe. Do not use `package`/`verify`/`install` for routine probing: those phases additionally trigger japicmp-maven-plugin (downloads previous released jsoup version, currently 1.23.1, from Maven Central for a binary-compat check that can break independent of the code under test), maven-javadoc-plugin, maven-bundle-plugin, central-publishing-maven-plugin. `mvn test` alone only runs surefire unit tests; failsafe integration tests (netty-based local webserver ITs) are bound to the `verify` phase and excluded by default via the failsafe.excludedGroups=long-running property, so a plain `mvn test` never needs netty ports.

JDK: pom.xml activates a `java-8` profile only when the running JDK is exactly 1.8, and a `multi-release` profile for JDK range [11,2000). JDK 9 or 10 activates neither profile and silently compiles nothing (default-compile/testCompile executions are disabled and no profile substitutes them) -- avoid those JDKs entirely. CI (.github/workflows/build.yml) matrix as of HEAD is java=[8,17,25] x os=[ubuntu,windows,macOS] running `mvn compile` then `mvn verify`. JDK 17 was chosen and verified for a 12-month mining window because it sits inside the multi-release band and is one of CI's own tested versions.

Network: no vendored deps, first build needs live Maven Central access (junit-jupiter 5.14.4, gson, netty-bom-managed artifacts, animal-sniffer-maven-plugin's java18 + toasttab gummy-bears-api-21 signatures, jacoco-maven-plugin). Do not pass -o/--offline unless the .m2 cache is already warm.

Entry points for call-graph construction (public API surface, this is a library with no main): org.jsoup.Jsoup static facade (parse* overloads, connect, newSession, clean*, isValid) in src/main/java/org/jsoup/Jsoup.java, and org.jsoup.select.Selector#select(String,Element) in src/main/java/org/jsoup/select/Selector.java. Also relevant but not yet method-verified: org.jsoup.nodes.Document/Element/Node instance API, org.jsoup.parser.Parser, org.jsoup.safety.Safelist/Cleaner.

Gap: forge_ci_status / GitHub API is returning HTTP 401 Bad credentials in this environment, so commit-history lookups to pick an older commit by date/tag are not possible via that tool. Only HEAD was actually probed; cross-history JDK validity for jsoup rests on CI-matrix + pom profile-activation reading, not a second probe.

subject: history tool windowing behaviour
body:
SUPERSEDES note_23babdd975c6186e, which claimed history_list_commits ignores 'since'. That claim is WRONG (or has since been fixed). Re-verified this run:

1. 'since' IS honoured by BOTH history_list_commits and history_candidates -- but it requires a FULL ISO-8601 INSTANT, not a bare date. since=2026-02-23 returns unknown{NotApplicable, "not an ISO-8601 instant: 2026-02-23"}. since=2026-02-23T00:00:00Z works. The prior note's author almost certainly passed bare dates, got NotApplicable or a silently unbounded result, and concluded the parameter was ignored. Always pass the Z-suffixed instant. 'until' takes the same form and also works (verified with a 2026-02-23T00:00:00Z..2026-03-09T00:00:00Z slice returning scanned=14, truncated=false).

2. Because 'since' works, you can get the EXACT commit count for a window in ONE call: set maxCount above the expected window size and read 'scanned' with truncated=false. For jsoup, since=2026-02-23T00:00:00Z + maxCount=400 gave scanned=138, truncated=false -- i.e. exactly 138 commits in the 6 months to HEAD 19c758e2. No need to bisect or to dump commit lists to estimate density.

3. Still true from the prior note: history_candidates' maxCount is SCAN DEPTH, not a cap on candidates returned, and there is no candidate-side cap parameter. But with 'since' working this matters much less -- bound the window by date and let maxCount be generously larger. A 138-commit window returning 104 non-control candidates plus 15 controls came back in a single response without truncation, so the size limit is not hit at this scale.

4. controlSampleSize draws from the commits matched by NO net. In the 138-commit window, 34 commits were unmatched and controlSampleSize=15 sampled 15 of those 34. So the control fraction is (sample / unmatched stratum), not (sample / window).

DENSITY, measured not estimated: jsoup commit activity is very bursty. 14 commits in 2026-02-23..03-09, only 2 in 2026-05-18..06-01, 13 in the 3 days 2026-08-20..08-23. Do not extrapolate window size from a recent slice -- the run-up to a release is many times the mid-cycle rate.

subject: jvm_build_probe ignores its commit parameter — do not trust per-commit builds
body:
Do not spend budget probing parent(f) and f expecting a real per-revision build gate. As of run_f7997c1a240cc238, jvm_build_probe (JvmHandlers.scala:137) reads only repoHandle and baseImage. The declared 'commit' parameter is never read. It compiles handles.dir(repoHandle) — the shared clone working tree — so it builds whatever is currently checked out.

Observed: four probes of four distinct commits (ccd90e9c, f10c02e1, be8c3756, 3475afc4) all returned buildHandle build_ade63ebfb3a3f8dc and left the clone at HEAD 19c758e2. registerBuild keys on (dir, baseImage), so the handle cannot distinguish revisions even in principle.

Attempted workaround that does NOT work: repo_checkout does create an isolated worktree at workspace/checkouts/<handle>_<commit12>, but jvm_build_probe has no parameter to point at it and always resolves the main clone dir. The two cannot be composed from the orchestrator.

Also: probes issued in parallel race on the one shared working tree, so concurrent probing is unsafe regardless.

Anything keyed on buildHandle inherits this — jvm_method_at_line, jvm_coverage_run, jvm_callgraph_build. Treat old-side line/method resolution and 'coverage at parent(f)' as unavailable until the handler takes a commit and builds an isolated worktree keyed on it. tools/check-params.mjs will NOT flag this: it concatenates all module sources and substring-matches the parameter name, so 'commit' being read by a different handler in the same file masks it.

Stages needing no build are unaffected: history_*, forge_*, szz_baseline all returned real per-commit data this run.

subject: jvm_build_probe flags parameter is a shell prefix, not build-tool flags
body: Passing flags:["-B","-q"] to jvm_build_probe makes the probe fail in 5s with COMPILE_ERROR, exitCode 2, stderrTail "sh: 0: Illegal option -B". BuildProbe assembles the container command as (flags ++ [cleanCommand,"&&"]? :+ buildCommand).mkString(" "), so flags are PREPENDED to the shell line, producing "-B -q mvn -B -q compile". The recipe's flags field is for shell-prefix tokens (env assignments), not maven switches. Put every maven switch inside `command` and omit `flags` entirely. With command="mvn -B -q compile" and no flags, jsoup compiles in ~55s on maven:3.9.9-eclipse-temurin-17. Note the failureClass is misleading here — it says COMPILE_ERROR, but nothing was compiled.

subject: Coverage reports parsed before the CoverageService minBy fix are unusable
body: Any jvm_coverage_lines result produced by a server built before the CoverageService merge fix under-reports coverage on multi-class source files: lines that are executed come back NOT_EXECUTABLE. Cause: per-class line entries were merged with maxBy(status.ordinal) over Covered(0)/Uncovered(1)/NotExecutable(2), so NotExecutable won. Each class spans getFirstLine..getLastLine, so an outer class with probes surrounding a nested class supplies empty entries across it and overwrites the real status. Symptom to recognize: a large file (parser state machine, connection helper, enum with anonymous constant bodies) shows a handful of COVERED lines and everything else NOT_EXECUTABLE, while small single-class files look normal. Do not compute faultyLinesCoveredFraction from such a report and do not treat the resulting zeros as evidence of untested code; re-run coverage against a server carrying the fix. jsoup files observed affected: HtmlTreeBuilderState.java, Token.java, HttpConnection.java. Unaffected: Cleaner.java, Re2jRegex.java, SimpleStreamReader.java, DataUtil.java, StringUtil.java.

subject: jvm_callgraph_build must be called serially — concurrent calls hang past the MCP idle timeout
body: Do not issue jvm_callgraph_build calls in parallel. Six concurrent builds against six distinct buildHandles (distinct worktrees, no shared checkout) returned two results and left four hanging with no progress until the client aborted them at ~1800s: "MCP server causeway tool jvm_callgraph_build sent no response or progress for 1800s". The two that returned did so normally (6575 nodes/29613 edges, 6439/28505), so the work itself is not slow — a solo build on this repo completes in well under a minute (7133 nodes/38232 edges at 46b62086). Distinct buildHandles are NOT enough to make these independent, so the contention is inside the call-graph service, not in the checkout layer. Contrast with jvm_build_probe, which parallelises fine at width 5 (~55-90s each) now that each revision gets its own worktree. Practical rule for S7 on a 19-bug run: probe in parallel, then build call graphs ONE AT A TIME. Budget cost of learning this the hard way: ~2 hours of wall clock for four aborted builds.

subject: S7 re-run recipe for run_f7997c1a240cc238 — order, concurrency limits, and the startup precondition
body:
Inputs are in runs/run_f7997c1a240cc238_s7_resume.tsv: 19 fix/parent pairs, the deterministic buildHandle each parent yields, and the old-side changed ranges per fix. All re-derivable from git; the file just saves the derivation.

STARTUP PRECONDITION, check this first. Main.scala:78 picks the ledger ONCE at startup: Neo4j reachable gives Neo4jEvidenceLedger (persistent) plus a live store, unreachable gives InMemoryEvidenceLedger and store=None, and GraphHandlers.withStore latches that None forever — there is no reconnect. A server started before the Neo4j container is therefore permanently unable to persist anything, and every evidenceId it issues dies with the process. Confirm Neo4j answers on bolt://localhost:7690 BEFORE the causeway server starts, and confirm exactly one causeway.app.Main process is running (two were observed after a host restart).

ORDER AND CONCURRENCY, learned by losing ~2h twice.
1. jvm_build_probe: parallel at width 5 is safe and fast (~55-90s each) now that each revision gets its own worktree. 19 parents in 4 waves.
2. jvm_coverage_run: sequential, ~115-231s each. The server pools these; do not parallelise.
3. jvm_coverage_lines: cheap, parallel is fine, and can be pipelined against the next coverage_run in the same block.
4. jvm_callgraph_build: STRICTLY ONE AT A TIME. See note_a3d07655a0ec21f1.

Worktrees under workspace/checkouts (38 of them) and the maven cache under workspace/caches survive restarts, so a re-probe is much cheaper than the first run. Coverage reports do NOT survive: they are parsed into a TrieMap in Handles and never written to disk.

Verification that the CoverageService merge fix is live before trusting any coverage number: at parent 46b620860af9, src/main/java/org/jsoup/parser/HtmlTreeBuilderState.java line 166 must come back COVERED. If it comes back NOT_EXECUTABLE the server is running a pre-fix jar and every fraction from it is garbage.

subject: jvm_callgraph_build wedges the ENTIRE JVM tool path after 3 builds per server process — not concurrency, not a bad revision
body:
SUPERSEDES note_a3d07655a0ec21f1 (which blamed concurrency) and CORRECTS runs/run_f7997c1a240cc238_s7_callgraph_finding.md (which blamed revision a682fd5b/build_d3aaa7f5c6f21591). Both are wrong. Serial execution does not help and no revision is special.

THE RULE: a causeway server process completes exactly 3 jvm_callgraph_build calls. The 4th hangs forever, and from that moment EVERY JVM-path tool in that process hangs forever too. Only a server restart clears it.

EVIDENCE, session e39d57d5, all calls strictly serial, one at a time:
  1. build_6b9d762cd7f4cbb1  OK  cg_000000001d26b901  6575 nodes / 29142 edges
  2. build_58aa4b07d486600c  OK  cg_000000006fa945a2  6573 / 29606
  3. build_5160088e81ec1f1a  OK  cg_000000007d1411b2  6439 / 28505
  4. build_bdfe2ee2e6db3574  HUNG, client aborted at 1804s

Prior session (eddff98b) ran the SAME first three, then a DIFFERENT 4th (build_d3aaa7f5c6f21591) — and it hung at the same position. Two sessions, two different 4th revisions, identical failure position. The revision is not the variable; the count is.

THE DISCRIMINATING TEST: after the hang I re-ran build_5160088e81ec1f1a — the very handle that had SUCCEEDED 20 minutes earlier as build #3. It hung (aborted 1800s). A revision that works at position 3 fails at position 5. This rules out any per-revision explanation.

SCOPE OF THE WEDGE IS NOT LIMITED TO CALL GRAPHS. After the hang, three jvm_method_at_line calls — a cheap debug-table lookup, no container, no analysis — all hung and aborted at ~1807s (build_6b9d762cd7f4cbb1, build_5160088e81ec1f1a, build_58aa4b07d486600c). So this is a shared executor being permanently consumed, not a call-graph-specific bug. Suspect the pool sized by CAUSEWAY_BUILD_SLOTS (currently 2 in .mcp.json): call-graph tasks appear to leak their slot rather than release it.

NON-JVM TOOLS SURVIVE. graph_resume_state answered normally after the wedge. graph_*, notes_*, repo_* are unaffected — you can still checkpoint and record honestly once the JVM side is dead.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR S7. 19 call graphs need ~7 server restarts at 3 per process. Do the JVM work in strict batches of 3 per server lifetime, and spend those 3 on the bugs you actually need (i.e. rank FIRST on coverage, then build graphs only for the --deep selection). Do NOT plan a 19-graph sweep in one process; it cannot finish. Also: jvm_build_probe is NOT affected — 19 probes ran at width 5 (53-85s each) before any call graph and all succeeded.

REFUTES the 'expensive revision' claim about a682fd5b: it compiled in 61s this session, against the 1465s reported in s7_callgraph_finding.md. That was host contention, not a property of the revision. Nothing about a682fd5b is unusual.

DATA-QUALITY CAVEAT: the same buildHandle yields different graph sizes across sessions. build_6b9d762cd7f4cbb1 gave 6159/27172 last session and 6575/29142 this one (~7% apart); build_58aa4b07d486600c gave 6577/29612 vs 6573/29606. Same entry points, same CHA algorithm. Treat nodeCount/edgeCount as approximate and do not compare blast radius across server processes.

subject: jvm_build_probe DOES isolate per commit now — the earlier 'ignores its commit parameter' note is stale
body:
SUPERSEDES note_eea1bc7b2ea4e132, which said jvm_build_probe ignores its `commit` parameter, always compiles the shared clone working tree, and returns one buildHandle (build_ade63ebfb3a3f8dc) for every revision — and concluded that "coverage at parent(f)" and old-side method/line resolution should be treated as UNAVAILABLE. That conclusion is no longer true and following it would wrongly discard this run's entire S7 result set.

WHAT CHANGED: each revision now gets its own worktree (see note_378bbab6b5f67656), so registerBuild's (dir, baseImage) key does distinguish revisions.

THE OBSERVATION THAT REFUTES THE OLD NOTE: 19 distinct parent commits produced 19 DISTINCT buildHandles, not one shared handle — e.g. 598a895a -> build_58aa4b07d486600c, 3475afc4 -> build_5160088e81ec1f1a, a682fd5b -> build_d3aaa7f5c6f21591, 46b62086 -> build_6b9d762cd7f4cbb1. The full table is runs/run_f7997c1a240cc238_s7_resume.tsv. Stronger still, these handles are DETERMINISTIC across server processes: session eddff98b predicted them, and session e39d57d5 re-ran all 19 probes from cold and reproduced every one EXACTLY. A handler that ignored `commit` could not produce 19 different handles, let alone the same 19 twice.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE FROM THE OLD NOTE: nothing about parallelism. The old note said concurrent probes race on one shared tree; with per-revision worktrees, width-5 parallel probing is safe and was measured at 53-85s each. The old note's warning against parallel probing is also stale.

STILL DO NOT ASSUME: this says nothing about jvm_callgraph_build, which has its own hard defect — 3 calls per server process, then the whole JVM tool path wedges permanently. See note_1a17e350ba889e71. That one is current and still binding.

Worktrees under workspace/checkouts and the maven cache under workspace/caches survive restarts, so re-probing is cheap. Coverage REPORTS do not survive a restart (parsed into an in-memory TrieMap); re-run jvm_coverage_run for any parent whose report you need to QUERY with jvm_coverage_lines.

subject: jvm_callgraph_build CRASHES the server (not just hangs), the client RESPAWNS it, and parallel JVM calls kill it too
body:
SUPERSEDES note_1a17e350ba889e71. That note was right that jvm_callgraph_build is the trigger and that ~3 per process is the ceiling. It was WRONG about two things that change the strategy completely.

CORRECTION 1 — IT CRASHES, IT DOES NOT ONLY HANG. Session 85d94556 saw the 3rd jvm_callgraph_build in a process return "Connection closed" and the java process disappear from the process table, rather than hanging for 1800s. Sometimes it hangs, sometimes it dies. Do not budget on the assumption you will get a clean 3.

CORRECTION 2 — THE SERVER COMES BACK BY ITSELF, AND THIS IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. The prior note said "only a server RESTART clears it" and treated that as terminal. In fact causeway is a stdio MCP child of the Claude Code client, and the client RESPAWNS it on the next tool call. Verified twice: after each crash, graph_resume_state answered normally and Neo4j-persisted state (checkpoints, findings) was fully intact. So a crash is recoverable, and the call-graph budget effectively RESETS per process.

WHAT A CRASH ACTUALLY COSTS: every in-memory handle. repoHandle, buildHandle, callGraphId, reportId all become "no clone registered" / unresolvable. Neo4j state survives; handle tables do not. Recovery is repo_clone (fast, returns the same deterministic repo_d914dc640c66633b) then jvm_build_probe per parent you need (~50-125s each on a warm cache, handles reproduce exactly).

CORRECTION 3 — PARALLELISM IS NOT SAFE FOR JVM TOOLS EITHER. Two jvm_method_at_line calls issued in the SAME message: one returned, the other came back "Connection closed" and took the process with it. The prior note only warned about parallel call-graph builds. Treat EVERY jvm_* call as strictly one-at-a-time. jvm_build_probe at width 4 also preceded a crash this session (4 concurrent probes, server gone afterwards) — the earlier claim that width 5 probing is safe is not reliable; use width 2 at most, and prefer serial.

THE PATTERN THAT ACTUALLY WORKS, and what the next session should do:
Build a graph and IMMEDIATELY extract what you need from it in the very next calls, one at a time. Do not build a graph and hand the callGraphId to a subagent — the handle will very likely be dead before the agent uses it. Extract jvm_callgraph_paths / jvm_callgraph_callers yourself, then pass the RESULTS (and their evidenceIds, which stay valid in the ledger forever) to the agent as text. This worked: 2 graphs built, both fully queried, all results preserved as citable evidence despite both handles now being dead.

CHEAPER SUBSTITUTE, use it first. If you only need to know WHICH METHOD a fault line sits in — and for a zero-hop or same-method bug that is the entire answer — jvm_method_at_line needs only a build probe, no call graph, and does not destabilise anything. Three of this run's five deep bugs were resolved this way for the cost of one probe each. Only spend a call graph when the entry point and the fault site are genuinely different methods AND the route between them is the thing you are trying to establish.

subject: shape of call paths out of org.jsoup.safety.Cleaner — two non-obvious hops are normal, not graph noise
body:
Hint for the next tracer working a Cleaner/Safelist bug; verify with tools before asserting.

Any path from Cleaner#clean(Document) down to the per-element cleaning logic is 6 hops, not 2, because of two structural detours that look like graph artifacts but are real:

1. Cleaner#copySafeNodes does NOT call the visitor directly. It goes through the DEFAULT INTERFACE METHOD org.jsoup.select.NodeVisitor#traverse(Node), which forwards to NodeTraversor#traverse(NodeVisitor,Node), which then calls back into Cleaner$CleaningVisitor#head. So expect an interface hop plus a traversal-utility hop in the middle of every Cleaner path. CHA resolves these fine; a trace-confined search would too, but do not be surprised by the length.

2. CleaningVisitor is a private INNER class calling private outer methods, so javac emits synthetic bridges (e.g. Cleaner#access$100). These appear as real nodes in the call graph. They carry no semantics — do not try to read a fault carrier out of them, and do not drop them from a reported path either, since they are genuine edges.

Practical consequence: when jvm_callgraph_paths is asked entry->fault inside safety/, a default maxLen of 12 is comfortable, but anything below 7 will return empty and read as DISCONNECTED when the code is in fact perfectly connected.

Also worth knowing before you go hunting for missing edges: the Cleaner's attribute logic spans three files, and reading only Cleaner.java will not explain behaviour. The admit/reject decision lives in Safelist#isSafeAttribute, and the actual storage semantics live in org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes. Budget three history_file_at reads, not one.

subject: jsoup issue bodies often name the regression-introducing commit; commit subjects understate bug fixes
body:
Two reusable observations from tracing b6fabf85 (NodeTraversor infinite loop, issue #2472).

1. REGRESSION PROVENANCE IS OFTEN IN THE ISSUE BODY, FREE.
jsoup reporters routinely write "Since <release>, this code will ... because of https://github.com/jhy/jsoup/commit/<sha>". Issue #2472's body names 967306fbd12dca9d465f3f1c47fbcad6cfe7531a outright. history_blame on the old-side fault lines at the parent independently attributed the single newly-added statement to that same sha. So for jsoup you frequently get a free SZZ cross-check: fetch forge_issue FIRST, scan the body for a commit URL, then confirm with history_blame rather than deriving the inducing commit from scratch. Worth doing before spending anything heavier.

2. COMMIT SUBJECTS UNDERSTATE. Do not adjudicate or explain from the subject line.
b6fabf85's subject is "Refactor NodeTraversor.traverse to have a clearer state machine impl" — reads NOT_BUG_FIX. The BODY says "Now if a node is replaced in head, we don't revisit it, so we won't loop" and "Fixes #2472", and #2472 is labelled bug/fixed. jhy tends to describe the mechanism (refactor, rewrite, simplify) in the subject and the defect in the body. Always pull the full message via history_commit_meta and read issueRefs; a subject-only heuristic will drop real fixes here.

3. Minor: history_blame at a parent SHA with side:"old" ranges lines up exactly with history_diff's oldRange numbering on this repo — verified line-by-line against history_file_at. No off-by-one to compensate for.

subject: jsoup IO faults propagate through pooled-buffer object state, so call-graph paths between parser entry points and DataUtil/internal stream code return zero by construction
body:
Hint, verify before asserting.

Do not spend budget widening maxLen or flipping direction when a path query between org.jsoup.parser.* (StreamParser, TreeBuilder, CharacterReader) and org.jsoup.helper.DataUtil / org.jsoup.internal.* comes back empty. In this area jsoup routinely passes a mutable stream object forward inside a struct rather than calling downward, so the corrupting write and the observing read genuinely share no call edge.

Concrete shape to expect:
- DataUtil.detectCharset returns a DataUtil.CharsetDoc struct holding {charset, doc, input}. Callers then choose ONE of the two payloads. DataUtil.parseInputStream(CharsetDoc,...) short-circuits on charsetDoc.doc; the streamParser callers discard doc and read charsetDoc.input. A defect that only damages one payload is invisible on the other consumer's tests even at 100% line coverage of the site.
- org.jsoup.internal.SimpleBufferedInput.close() releases its byte[] to a static SoftPool and sets byteBuf = null (source comment: "NPE further attempts to read"), but does NOT reset bufPos/bufLength. Its getBuf() is Validate.notNull(byteBuf), the SINGLE-ARG overload, so the user-visible failure is ValidationException("Object must not be null") with no descriptive text and, in issue reports, usually no stack frames. If you see that exact message anywhere in jsoup, suspect a stream closed while its logical buffer still had unread bytes, and look for the close, not for the read.
- ControllableInputStream.allowClose(false)/(true) brackets a speculative parse. A close() that is a no-op inside the bracket becomes real after the finally block. Reads of that code that ignore the bracket will misplace the fault.

Practical consequence for tracing: anchor the fault with jvm_method_at_line on old-side lines as usual, take the one static hop that does exist (caller -> DataUtil.detectCharset), and then trace the rest by reading source with history_file_at. Report the entry->fault leg and the fault->symptom leg as distinct relationships with distinct tiers rather than averaging them into one number; the honest overall tier for these routes is DISCONNECTED with pathFidelity PARTIAL.

Also: the JVM tool path (jvm_callgraph_*, jvm_method_at_line, jvm_method_body) was unavailable for the whole of run_f7997c1a240cc238; handles die and jvm_callgraph_build crashes the server. history_* and forge_* were unaffected and were sufficient to establish every hop of a state-mediated route at method granularity.

subject: shape of the org.jsoup.internal stream stack - one hop is an inherited JDK frame and is invisible without a call graph
body:
Derived while tracing 49e58c20 (spurious available() throws, issue #2474). Re-derivable only by reading three files, so recording the shape.

THE STACK, parent-commit shape (verified by history_file_at at b77e51ba):
  SimpleStreamReader (extends Reader; field `in` is an InputStream)
    -> ControllableInputStream (extends FilterInputStream; private field `buff` is "super.in, but typed as SimpleBufferedInput")
      -> SimpleBufferedInput (extends FilterInputStream; wraps the caller's raw stream)
        -> the caller's raw InputStream

WHO BUILDS IT: DataUtil.detectCharset does `new SimpleStreamReader(input, UTF_8)` where `input` is the ControllableInputStream; DataUtil.streamParser does the same with charsetDoc.input. DataUtil.load(InputStream,...) and DataUtil.openStream(Path) both funnel through ControllableInputStream.wrap(in, 0), which constructs `new ControllableInputStream(new SimpleBufferedInput(in), maxSize)`. So in every parse path SimpleStreamReader.in is a ControllableInputStream.

THE TRAP: ControllableInputStream OVERRIDES read(byte[],int,int), reset, mark, markSupported and close, but does NOT override available(). So any available() call from SimpleStreamReader lands on the INHERITED java.io.FilterInputStream#available(), which delegates to the SimpleBufferedInput passed to super(in). That middle frame exists in no jsoup source file. Expect it to be missing or to look like a broken edge in any call-graph result; it is not graph noise and it is not DISCONNECTED-by-reflection. Same trap applies to ControllableInputStream#read, which calls `super.read(...)` rather than buff.read(...) - the SimpleBufferedInput hop again goes through an inherited FilterInputStream frame.

CONSEQUENCE FOR EVIDENCE: a route through this stack cannot be made FULL fidelity from source reading alone, because the FilterInputStream delegation is JDK-internal and not retrievable with the history tools. The jsoup-side facts (no override present, ctor passes the wrapped stream to super) ARE retrievable and are the strongest available backing. Record the JDK hop as a gap rather than asserting it.

ALSO USEFUL: ControllableInputStream#read narrows its catch to SocketTimeoutException inside its retry loop, so a plain IOException from lower in the stack propagates. Do not assume the wrapper swallows IO errors.

Cross-check that paid off here: issue #2474's body named the exact failing CI test (ConnectTest.maxBodySize on JDK 8 Ubuntu) and the exact throwing API, for free, before any heavier tool. Consistent with the existing CONVENTION note about jsoup issue bodies.

subject: graph_upsert_bug silently drops nested fields, and graph_query bugCount keys on repo not runId
body:
Two traps that cost this run a full round of re-writes. Both are silent — neither produces an error.

TRAP 1 — graph_upsert_bug reads only EIGHT TOP-LEVEL fields from `record`, and discards everything else without complaint. The fields it actually persists (GraphHandlers.scala putBug call) are: repo, fixSha, admitted, rejectedFor, importance, scoredOn, reproducerTier, pathFidelity. That is the whole of it.

Everything else you put in `record` — symptom, faultSite, path, metrics, evidence, gaps, buildGate — is accepted, echoed back as {created:true, relationshipsWritten:2}, and DROPPED. The response looks like a full success in every case.

The specific way this bites: reproducerTier and pathFidelity are read with str(rec, "reproducerTier") / str(rec, "pathFidelity"), i.e. TOP LEVEL. It is natural to nest them as record.reproducer.tier and record.path.fidelity, because that is how the data is shaped everywhere else in the pipeline. Do that and both persist as null while the call still reports success. This run wrote all 19 bugs that way and had to re-upsert the deep 5 to fix it. The MERGE is idempotent on (repo, fixSha), so a corrective re-upsert is cheap and safe — but you have to notice first.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHERE THE REAL DATA LIVES: the rich per-bug detail does NOT live on the Bug node. It lives in the findings recorded by findings_record, whose full claim JSON IS persisted verbatim. Treat graph_upsert_bug as an index (which bugs, admitted or not, at what tier) and findings as the payload. export_run reads BugRow, so the export inherits the same eight fields.

TRAP 2 — graph_query "bugCount" and "rejectionBreakdown" take params.REPO, not params.runId. Passing {"runId": "run_..."} is accepted and returns {total: 0, admitted: 0} / an empty breakdown — a perfectly plausible answer that is simply the count for repo "". Pass {"repo": "jhy/jsoup"}. With the right param this run returned total 19, admitted 19. If a bugCount of 0 ever contradicts upserts you just watched succeed, check the param name before concluding the writes failed.

MINOR, but do not report it as fact: the handler hardcodes created:true and relationshipsWritten:2 in its response. Those are constants, not measurements — a MERGE that updated an existing node still reports created:true. Do not cite "created" as evidence that a bug was new.

subject: jvm_native_test_run reports a VACUOUS failsAtParent=false when the fix ADDS its regression test — rung 1 cannot yield T1 on jsoup as the tool currently stands
body:
Hint, verify before asserting. Cost one 351s container run to discover.

WHAT HAPPENED: jvm_native_test_run on fix 84ca201d with selector
W3CDomTest#preservesProcessingInstructions+preservesDocumentLevelComments+preservesCdataSections
returned ok:true with failsAtParent=false, passesAtFix=true, differs=false, no traceId.
Read naively that says "the project's own regression test does not capture the bug", which is
false. The parent-side output says "Tests run: 0 ... BUILD SUCCESS". The selector matched
NOTHING at the parent.

WHY: all three methods are ADDED by the fix. They do not exist at parent 598a895a. Verified by
git: 0 of 3 present at parent, 3 of 3 at the fix. The same holds for ALL FIVE deep bugs of this
run — 7c32b7e1 (0/3), 823709f5 (0/1), b6fabf85 (0/4), 84ca201d (0/3), 49e58c20 (0/1).

TWO SEPARATE CAUSES, do not conflate them:

1. HANDLER GUARD IS TOO NARROW. AnalysisHandlers.scala nativeTestRun has
   `if !r.parent.ran && !r.fix.ran then Unknown(TestsFailed)`. The AND means the guard only
   fires when NEITHER side ran. The added-test case is parent.ran=false, fix.ran=true, so it
   falls through to the data branch, where failsAtParent is computed as
   `r.parent.ran && !r.parent.passed` = false. The comment directly above the guard describes
   exactly this hazard ("reporting it as 'does not reproduce' would blame the bug for a typo")
   and the condition does not implement it. NativeTestRunner itself is NOT at fault: ranAnyTest
   correctly returns false on "Tests run: 0", and differs correctly requires parent.ran.

2. NO TEST PORTING. Even with the guard fixed, the result would be Unknown, not T1.
   NativeTestRunner.differential(parentTree, fixTree, ...) runs each revision's own worktree
   as-is. For a fix that ADDS a regression test — which is the overwhelmingly common shape, and
   the shape the tool's own description assumes ("It should FAIL at the parent") — the test is
   simply absent at the parent. Rung 1 can only ever fire today when a fix MODIFIES a test that
   already existed. Defects4J-style differential testing ports the fix's test files onto the
   buggy revision first; this tool does not.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NEXT AGENT: do NOT interpret differs=false from this tool as
evidence a bug lacks a native reproducer until you have checked that the selector actually ran
at the PARENT. The response does not expose a `ran` flag, so the only way to tell is to read
resultAtParent for "Tests run: 0". If resultAtParent is absent entirely (the handler only emits
it when parent.detail is non-empty) you cannot tell at all from the response.

CHEAP PRECHECK, do this before spending ~6 minutes per call: `git show <parent>:<testfile> |
grep -c <methodName>`. Zero means rung 1 will be vacuous for that selector.

subject: Rung 1 requires the ported test to COMPILE at the parent — a regression test exercising an API the fix introduced can NEVER convert, and file-granular porting spreads that failure across the whole module
body:
A property of the reproducer ladder, not of jsoup. Worth knowing before the next repository.

THE RULE: rung 1 ports the fix's test sources onto the parent worktree and runs them there. That
only works if the ported test COMPILES against the PARENT's production code. Where a fix adds
both a defect repair AND the API its regression test calls, the test can never run at the parent,
so the bug can never reach T1_NATIVE. No selector, no retry and no timeout change helps. This is
structural.

MEASURED IN run_f7997c1a240cc238, 2 of 14 bugs, both confirmed by git:
- 4e381147 (RFC 9110 redirect methods): HttpConnectionTest#redirectMethodsFollowHttpSemantics
  calls HttpConnection.redirectMethod(int,Method). Occurrences in HttpConnection.java: 0 at the
  parent, 2 at the fix.
- b035b623 (hostless HTTP URLs): the new StringUtilTest methods call StringUtil.isHttpScheme and
  StringUtil.hasHttpScheme. Both 0 at the parent.

HOW IT PRESENTS: Unknown(TestsFailed) with detail "ran no test at the parent (ported test did not
run there)". That is the CORRECT answer and it is citable. Do not read it as a broken selector
before checking whether the test calls something the fix introduced. Cheap check, no container:
  git show <fix>:<testfile> | grep -oE '<ClassUnderTest>\\.[a-zA-Z0-9_]+'
then grep each symbol in the parent's production file; a zero means this note applies.

THE AMPLIFIER, and the part that cost an extra attempt: PORTING IS FILE-GRANULAR. Every test file
the fix touched is overlaid, not just the file holding the selector. Maven compiles all test
sources as one unit, so ONE uncompilable ported file fails the whole test compile and NO selector
in ANY file can run. On 4e381147 the behavioural ConnectTest methods do not touch the new API and
would have run happily, but HttpConnectionTest.java was ported alongside and broke the compile.
Same on b035b623, where the CleanerTest methods (dropsHostlessUrls, checksPreservedLinks,
resolvesSameSchemeUrl) were unreachable for the same reason.

POSSIBLE IMPROVEMENT, not implemented: port only the test files needed by the selector's class
(plus shared helpers). That would likely recover 4e381147 and possibly part of b035b623. It is not
free — test files reference shared fixtures and base classes, so "needed by" is not simply one
file — which is why it was left alone rather than guessed at.

RELATED, and now DISPROVEN, so do not repeat it: "the test needs a network" is NOT a reason to
avoid a selector here. NativeTestRunner.runSide passes network=true, and an in-container loopback
server works regardless of the --network none convention used elsewhere in the pipeline. jsoup's
ConnectTest, which starts a netty webserver, ran fine and bound localhost:40739 inside the
container (9d2241ff, ev_9744bd3a62e7a9d0f23f6d2fa5fa6f6d). An earlier note in this run preferred
DataUtilTest over ConnectTest on that reasoning; the reasoning was wrong.

subject: no buildHandle/callGraphId exists for parent 209151fddc9ea1be665176a5dd142ab68260af48 (5ee2e11a fix)
body:
Tracing 5ee2e11a8f5b6f3c32b7edef246d5623223aa53e (W3CDom NPE on invalid XML element names) against its parent 209151fddc9ea1be665176a5dd142ab68260af48: no note in this run records a buildHandle for this specific parent (known handles cover 598a895a, e640ca8a, f727535b, b77e51ba, 46b620860af9, 19c758e2...; none match 209151fd). Path-tracer is not granted jvm_build_probe or jvm_callgraph_build, so jvm_method_at_line/jvm_method_body/jvm_callgraph_paths/jvm_class_hierarchy could not be called for this commit at all.

Workaround used successfully: history_file_at at the exact parent sha to read source and pin old-side line numbers by eye (fast, unambiguous for this single well-commented file), plus jvm_trace_executed(traceId tr_c78a574b29d8aaab, packageFilter org.jsoup.helper / org.jsoup.select) to score OBSERVED/UNOBSERVED per hop — that tool needs neither buildHandle nor callGraphId.

Confirmed fault mechanism (source-level, not debug-info-verified): W3CDom$W3CBuilder#w3cSafeName(String,Syntax) returned null at old-side line ~513 when Attribute.getValidKey rejected a name outright (digit/hyphen-leading tag names, reachable via el.tagName("1abc") DOM mutation). The one existing caller (setAttribute, old line 476) already null-checked it; the element-name caller in W3CBuilder#head (old line 376 assigns, old line 379 dereferences via `tagName.contains(":")`) did not, causing the observed NPE. Both head() and w3cSafeName() are confirmed present in tr_c78a574b29d8aaab's executed set.

Surprising trace result worth flagging: the S9 entry point W3CDom#fromJsoup(Document) is ABSENT from tr_c78a574b29d8aaab's org.jsoup.helper executed set (21/21 methods returned, not truncated) even though it's the statically-expected overload for the test's Document-typed local, and its one-line delegate fromJsoup(Element) IS present. Similarly org.jsoup.select.NodeVisitor#traverse(Node) (the default interface method invoked via builder.traverse(rootEl)) is absent from the complete 44-method org.jsoup.select executed set even though the only viable static route to the confirmed-executed NodeTraversor#traverse(NodeVisitor,Node) runs through it. subject: jvm_trace_executed appears to under-report trivial one-line delegating/casting methods
body:
While tracing 3475afc4 (Attributes internal-attribute CCE, traceId tr_edff3850a86229d5) both org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes#checkNotNull(Object) and org.jsoup.nodes.Element#select(String) were confirmed ABSENT from a full, non-truncated org.jsoup.nodes packageFilter trace (61 methods), despite:
  - checkNotNull being the ONLY callee of getIgnoreCase(String)'s ternary (`return i==NotFound ? EmptyString : checkNotNull(vals[i]);`), and getIgnoreCase itself IS present in the same trace;
  - Element#select(String) being the conventional one-line wrapper (`return Selector.select(cssQuery, this);`) that doc.select(...) must go through to ever reach org.jsoup.select.Selector#select(String,Element), which IS present in the trace.

Both missing methods are single-statement bodies (a ternary+cast, and a direct delegate). Both their unambiguous callers/callees ARE present. This is NOT the JaCoCo synthetic-bridge/lambda case described in the general tracer guidance — lambda-desugared methods (e.g. org.jsoup.select.Evaluator#lambda$asPredicate$0) DID show up in this same trace, so lambdas are not blanket-excluded here.

Working hypothesis, NOT verified: the trace instrument may record a method as "executed" only on some condition tied to bytecode shape (e.g. a JaCoCo-style branch/line probe placement) that a trivial one-statement method doesn't satisfy, independent of whether it throws. Do not assume a method absent from jvm_trace_executed was never called — check whether its only caller is present and whether its body is a single statement before treating the absence as a real "this code path was not exercised" signal. Record such hops as UNOBSERVED (not UNMEASURABLE — they're ordinary non-synthetic non-JDK methods) and cross-check with history_file_at for the call site.

subject: JaCoCo traces systematically OMIT trivial methods that exited via a propagating exception — these hops are UNMEASURABLE, not unobserved, and the bias falls hardest on EXCEPTION-channel bugs
body:
Verify before asserting, but this was established by a controlled comparison, not inferred.

THE EFFECT: jvm_trace_executed reports a method as executed only when a JaCoCo probe FIRES. Probes
sit at branch targets and at method exit. A method that is ENTERED and then exited ABNORMALLY,
because an exception propagated through it, and that has no probe before the throw point, fires
NOTHING and is reported as NOT EXECUTED. Straight-line one-statement methods — delegating
overloads, default interface methods, tiny helpers — are exactly the shape with a single exit
probe, so they are exactly the ones that vanish.

THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON that establishes it, same method, same body, two runs:
  org.jsoup.helper.W3CDom#fromJsoup(org.jsoup.nodes.Document) is `return fromJsoup((Element) in);`
  and exists identically at both parents (line 184 at 598a895a and at 209151fd).
   - tr_bd0969f99798ad76 (bug 84ca201d, ASSERTION channel, no exception unwinds through it):
     PRESENT in the executed set (ev_99abb1fa002e803d5476304399c6b8bc).
   - tr_c78a574b29d8aaab (bug 5ee2e11a, NullPointerException propagates through it):
     ABSENT (ev_9e379c5c09b24fbe442bde2f80a86da0), while its own callee fromJsoup(Element) and
     the deeper convert() ARE present.
  The difference is not the method and not the class. It is whether an exception unwound through it.

SECOND INSTANCE, same shape: org.jsoup.nodes.Attributes#checkNotNull is
`return val == null ? EmptyString : (String) val;` at be8c3756 line 124, called unconditionally
from getIgnoreCase line 136, and it is the frame that THREW the ClassCastException in bug
3475afc4. It is absent from tr_edff3850a86229d5 even though it demonstrably ran.

WHY DEEPER FRAMES SURVIVE AND SHALLOW ONES DO NOT: a method containing branches or loops fires
probes BEFORE the exception occurs further down, so it still registers. That is why in 5ee2e11a
convert() and fromJsoup(Element) appear while the one-line fromJsoup(Document) does not. Absence
therefore correlates with METHOD SHAPE plus exception path, not with call depth.

HOW TO SCORE IT, and this is the part that changes numbers:
Classify such a hop UNMEASURABLE, in the same bucket as javac synthetic bridges (access$100,
lambda$...) and JDK-internal frames outside the instrumented class dirs. Do NOT call it
UNOBSERVED. Unobserved should mean "the instrument could have reported this and did not, so the
route probably did not run". Here the instrument CANNOT report it even in principle. Treating the
two alike understates the observed fraction, and it understates it selectively on
CRASH_UNCAUGHT_EXCEPTION and other EXCEPTION-channel bugs — precisely the bugs whose propagation
route is most interesting. Do not silently promote them to observed either; report the two
categories side by side and let the reader see the split.

CHEAP TEST when a statically unavoidable method is missing from a trace: read its body at the
parent with history_file_at. If it is straight-line with no branch, and the run failed by a thrown
exception that passed through it, this note applies. If it has branches and is still missing, that
is a different and unexplained problem worth reporting.

CONSEQUENCE FOR TIERING: do not demote a whole route to HYPOTHESIZED merely because unmeasurable
hops appear in it. A route whose every MEASURABLE hop is observed, with the remainder unmeasurable
for this structural reason, is better reported as OBSERVED with an explicit unmeasurable count.

subject: AMENDS note_0d737bf5d478c0c8 — the exception-exit omission is real but NOT permanent: it was jvm_native_test_run failing to implement D27, now fixed, and the frames recover those hops
body:
READ note_0d737bf5d478c0c8 FIRST. It is deliberately NOT superseded: its mechanism is correct and
worth knowing. This note corrects only its CONCLUSION.

WHAT THAT NOTE GOT RIGHT: JaCoCo marks a method executed only when a probe fires, so a
straight-line method entered and exited abnormally by a propagating exception fires nothing and is
absent from a COVERAGE-ONLY executed set. The controlled comparison it records
(W3CDom#fromJsoup(Document) present in an assertion trace, absent in an NPE trace) stands.

WHAT IT GOT WRONG: it concluded those hops are UNMEASURABLE — that the instrument cannot report
them even in principle. That was never true. It was a missing implementation.

D27 already specifies that the executed set is coverage UNION the throw's stack-trace frames,
precisely because a method that throws records no probe. jvm_harness_run implemented it via
framesOf. jvm_native_test_run did NOT. The gap was in the tool, not the instrument.

NOW FIXED, and measured: NativeTestRunner parses ordinary Java stack traces out of the build
tool's own output and unions them with coverage, deduplicating by class and name (D27's rule,
since a stack trace carries no descriptor). Frame-derived methods are identifiable in
jvm_trace_executed output by an EMPTY descriptor. The response also reports frameMethodCount, how
many methods the frames contributed that coverage lacked.

RE-RUN RESULTS on the EXCEPTION-channel bugs, all previously "unmeasurable" hops recovered:
- 3475afc4: Attributes#checkNotNull — the frame that actually threw the ClassCastException — now
  present (ev_90b210e0b955450cd4c1658e491fb680). Path went 9/10 observed to 10/10.
- 5ee2e11a: NodeVisitor#traverse now present (ev_1c7eda9105480b4e528ef5e04af42043). Path went
  3/6 observed to 6/6, and the tier is OBSERVED on evidence.
- frameMethodCount by bug: 9d2241ff 74 (deep java.net stacks), 3475afc4 13, b035b623 12,
  49e58c20 5, and 4 each for 5ee2e11a, 823709f5, cad054a6.

THE CATEGORY STILL EXISTS, just much smaller. Two things frames do NOT recover:
1. javac synthetic accessor bridges (access$100, lambda$...). JaCoCo omits them and they will not
   appear in a stack trace unless they happen to be on the stack when something throws. 7c32b7e1
   still carries 2 genuinely unmeasurable hops for this reason, and it is an ASSERTION-channel bug
   so nothing unwound.
2. Anything on an ASSERTION-channel run generally: no exception, no frames, so coverage alone is
   still all you get. The union helps EXCEPTION-channel bugs specifically.

AND THE FIX DISCRIMINATES CORRECTLY, which is the real test: on 49e58c20 the union did NOT
recover SimpleStreamReader#read or SimpleBufferedInput#available, so that path's 0-of-2 observed
score STANDS. Those endpoints were genuinely never executed — the reproducer enters at
DataUtil.parseInputStream. A tool that recovered them would have been papering over a real
negative.

CAVEAT WORTH CARRYING: D27 matches by class and name only, so OVERLOADS COLLIDE. On 5ee2e11a the
hop fromJsoup(Document) -> fromJsoup(Element) has both endpoints resolving to the one key
W3CDom.fromJsoup. It scores observed under that rule and the overloads are not distinguishable.
That is D27's stated tradeoff — demanding descriptors would empty the intersection instead — but
record it rather than glossing it when a hop's two ends share a name.

subject: b035b623 (#2579 hostless URL): StringUtil#resolve(URL,String) absent from trace despite being the only reachable branch of resolve(String,String)
body:
Tracing b035b623d3d1d0c50 (parent ae8c6d21f), tr_64b8508d94bf4c84, packageFilter=org.jsoup.internal (25 methods, non-truncated): StringUtil#resolve(String,String) appears with full descriptor (Ljava/lang/String;Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/lang/String; -- a genuine coverage hit, not a frame recovery. Its sibling overload resolve(URL,String) (descriptor (Ljava/net/URL;Ljava/lang/String;)Ljava/net/URL;) does NOT appear anywhere in the same filtered result, even though source at the parent shows resolve(String,String) calling it unconditionally whenever the baseUrl parses (`return resolve(base, relUrl).toExternalForm();`), and the reproducer's base 'http://example.com/a/b' always parses successfully -- so this is the only reachable branch, not a rare one. stripControlChars (called at entry of both overloads) IS present in the trace, reinforcing that the omission is specific to resolve(URL,String) and not a general internal-package gap.

This extends the existing under-report note (note_84c7fb7df882e698, which was about trivial one-line delegates) to a NON-trivial, multi-statement, control-flow-bearing method. Do not assume absence from jvm_trace_executed means a substantial method didn't run just because it isn't a one-liner -- check whether the only caller is present and whether the source's control flow leaves any other branch possible before concluding UNOBSERVED reflects reality rather than an instrumentation gap. Per the general scoring rule still record it as UNOBSERVED (full, non-truncated retrieval; endpoint genuinely absent), but flag the source-level contradiction explicitly rather than silently reporting a clean UNOBSERVED.

Separately: this bug's true fault (missing host validation for HTTP(S) resolution results) is an ABSENT GUARD at the parent -- there is no statement to instrument, so no trace tier could ever surface it directly regardless of the above. Treat "the guarded method ran but the guard doesn't exist yet" as the default shape for assertion-channel bugs on this repo, not a special case.

subject: Exception-exit frames and overload collisions in jvm_native_test_run traces — what the executed set does and does not contain, measured
body:
SUPERSEDES note_0d737bf5d478c0c8, whose MECHANISM was right and CONCLUSION wrong. It called the
missing hops "unmeasurable", a property of JaCoCo. They were a property of the TOOL:
jvm_native_test_run had never implemented D27. It does now, and the frames recover them. Also
replaces the interim amendment note_c979d74b35973f91.

STILL TRUE. JaCoCo marks a method executed only when a probe fires, and probes sit at branch
targets and method exits. A straight-line method entered and exited ABNORMALLY by a propagating
exception fires nothing and is absent from a COVERAGE-ONLY set. Controlled comparison:
W3CDom#fromJsoup(Document), body `return fromJsoup((Element) in);`, identical at both parents —
PRESENT in an assertion-failure trace, ABSENT in an NPE trace. Methods with internal branches
survive, because probes fire before the exception occurs deeper; that is why convert() appeared
and the one-line fromJsoup(Document) did not.

THE FIX. D27 already specified executed = coverage UNION the throw's stack frames.
jvm_harness_run implemented it via framesOf; jvm_native_test_run did not. It now parses ordinary
Java stack traces from build-tool output and unions them. Frame-derived entries have an EMPTY
descriptor; the response reports frameMethodCount.

RECOVERED, measured:
- 3475afc4: Attributes#checkNotNull, the frame that THREW the ClassCastException, now present
  (ev_90b210e0b955450cd4c1658e491fb680). Path 9/10 observed -> 10/10.
- 5ee2e11a: NodeVisitor#traverse now present (ev_1c7eda9105480b4e528ef5e04af42043). 3/6 -> 6/6.
- frameMethodCount: 9d2241ff 74 (deep java.net stacks), 4e381147 26, 3475afc4 13, b035b623 12,
  49e58c20 5, and 4 each for 5ee2e11a, 823709f5, cad054a6.

GENUINELY UNRECOVERABLE, expect these to survive any tooling: javac SYNTHETIC ACCESSOR BRIDGES
(access$100, lambda$...). JaCoCo omits them and they reach a stack trace only if on the stack when
something throws. The only unmeasurable hops left in this run are the two either side of
Cleaner#access$100 in 7c32b7e1 — an ASSERTION-channel bug, so nothing unwound and no frames
existed. That is the shape: a synthetic bridge on a non-throwing run. More broadly, an
assertion-channel run produces no frames at all, so the union helps EXCEPTION-channel bugs only.

IT DISCRIMINATES CORRECTLY, the real test. On 49e58c20 the union did NOT recover
SimpleStreamReader#read or SimpleBufferedInput#available, so that path's 0-of-2 score STANDS:
those were genuinely never executed, the reproducer enters at DataUtil.parseInputStream. A tool
that "recovered" them would have hidden a true negative.

SECOND TRAP, found while fixing the first. The union was first written as groupBy((fqcn,name))
over coverage ++ frames. D27's class-and-name rule governs MATCHING ACROSS PRODUCERS; applying it
to the RESULT destroys overload precision coverage HAD. Symptom: one StringUtil#resolve entry
representable, and a tracer scored resolve(String,String) -> resolve(URL,String) UNOBSERVED when
the trace simply could not tell. Same hid HttpConnection$Response#execute's two overloads. Fixed
by keeping coverage entries verbatim and appending only frames whose (class,name) coverage lacked.
Both overload pairs then appeared distinctly (ev_9fe41ec8641e794581d430c5d1836f1c,
ev_677120b141f03f8304067134cdb5fe61) and both paths re-scored OBSERVED.

RESIDUAL COLLISION, unavoidable: a FRAME-derived method has no descriptor, so if coverage never
saw it and it shares a name with a covered overload, it is not appended and the two stay
indistinguishable. 5ee2e11a's fromJsoup(Document) -> fromJsoup(Element) is exactly this — it
scores observed under class-and-name matching and the overloads cannot be told apart. Say so on
such a hop rather than reporting it clean.
